title: Safety Boundaries
outcome: By the end, I can explain safety boundaries using a traced example and a stated limitation.
scenario: Make a strict lookup identifier boundary visible.
given: Toy lookup accepts exactly two uppercase ASCII letters followed by one digit. Accepted example: AB7. No trimming or extra characters are allowed.
All inputs and outcomes in this worked example are invented classroom data; no real model run is claimed.

steps.label: Check pattern
steps.detail: AB7 has two permitted letters and one digit, with no extra characters.

steps.label: Reject extra text
steps.detail: AB7; send() violates the exact identifier pattern.

steps.label: Separate authority
steps.detail: Pattern acceptance only allows the next lookup check; it grants no access to restricted records.

explanation: Read the picture in order. Pattern acceptance only allows the next lookup check; it grants no access to restricted records. The arrows show which recorded input or intermediate result each decision uses. Explain the deciding step aloud before checking the changed case; pointing to the final answer alone does not show how it follows.

counterfactual.prediction: Reject it under the exact uppercase rule.
counterfactual.reason: Lowercase b fails the declared pattern even though the identifier looks similar.

student_task: If AB7 passes the pattern, may it access teacher-only material? Point to the relevant step in the picture, then write the changed result and the rule or evidence that supports it.
teacher_answer: Not from pattern validity alone. The server must separately enforce the authenticated user’s access rights. Changed-case check: Reject it under the exact uppercase rule. Lowercase b fails the declared pattern even though the identifier looks similar.
project_evidence: For your Verified Study Buddy, save the input, procedure, observed result and limitation of this check. Label this worked example as practice; use a different, previously unreviewed case when checking independent understanding.
limits: Strict formatting is one boundary; it does not solve every injection or authorisation problem.
review_note: Reviewed Safety Boundaries against the assigned lesson pack and its reserved independent case. Added a different explicit worked scenario, an auditable trace and a changed-input check; preserved the original curriculum and assessment boundary.
